strategies.name: Hedging risk with futures
strategies.desc: Offset market risk in a stock or portfolio by shorting index futures in proportion to its beta (the minimum-variance hedge ratio).
strategies.adapted_note: Index spot returns proxy futures returns.

signal.label: Hedge a ₹100 portfolio of NIFTY 50 stocks with ≈ ₹98 of index futures short
signal.detail: Short futures notional = β × portfolio value (minimum-variance hedge ratio h* = ρσₛ/σₐ)

tables.title: Minimum-variance hedge of each stock with NIFTY 50 futures (252d)

notes: Strategy curve = equal-weight basket of all 50 constituents minus a short in NIFTY 50 futures sized at the rolling 252-day regression β (estimated out-of-sample, lagged one day). The benchmark curve is the unhedged basket. The hedged line keeps the stock-selection residual but removes market direction.
Spot index returns proxy the futures returns (no futures data on Yahoo Finance); contract lot sizes, basis and roll costs are not modelled.

strategies.name: Cross-hedging
strategies.desc: Hedge an exposure that has no futures of its own (sector index, other broad index) using index futures on a correlated underlying, with the hedge ratio from regression.
strategies.adapted_note: Index spot returns proxy futures returns.

signal.label: Hedge Nifty Bank with β = 1.12 × NIFTY 50 futures
signal.detail: Optimal hedge ratio estimated by regression; basis risk = unexplained residual

tables.title: Cross-hedging assets that have no liquid futures, using NIFTY 50 futures

notes: Strategy curve = Nifty Bank minus βₜ₋₁ × NIFTY 50 (rolling 252-day β, out-of-sample); benchmark = unhedged Nifty Bank. Cross-hedging (Eq. 463) uses futures on a different but correlated underlying, so a basis-risk residual remains. Sector indices (and the other broad index) have no or thin futures, so the NIFTY/SENSEX futures are the practical hedge.
Spot returns proxy futures returns; lot-size rounding, basis and rolls are not modelled.

Cross-hedging (Eq. 463) uses futures on a different but correlated underlying, so a basis-risk residual remains. Sector indices (and the other broad index) have no or thin futures, so the NIFTY/SENSEX futures are the practical hedge.
Spot returns proxy futures returns; lot-size rounding, basis and rolls are not modelled.

strategies.name: Contrarian trading (mean-reversion)
strategies.desc: Within a universe of futures, buy last week's relative losers and sell last week's relative winners, scaling positions by 1/volatility.
strategies.adapted_note: Single-stock futures proxied by spot stock returns.

signal.label: Long Nestle India, Tata Motors, Shriram Finance, NTPC +24 | Short Wipro, Tech Mahindra, Tata Consultancy Services, HCL Technologies +18

tables.title: Target portfolio now (rebalance at the latest close)

notes: Contrarian weights wᵢ = −γ (Rᵢ − Rₘ)/σᵢ on 1-week returns, where Rₘ is the equal-weighted market return of the universe (Eqs. 469-471). The book's suggested 1/σ suppression is applied so volatile names are not over-invested. Applied to the constituents' single-stock futures (spot returns as proxy). This is the futures-market twin of 3.9, with volatility scaling.

Rebalanced weekly with 10 bps one-way cost; weights are scaled to unit gross exposure. 'Sharpe (gross)' ignores costs. The dashed line is the index buy-and-hold; 'long only' holds only the positive weights.
Shorting single stocks in India is done through stock futures (F&O stocks) or intraday; borrow, margin and slippage are not modelled.

strategies.name: Trend following (momentum)
strategies.desc: Go long the futures that have been trending up relative to the market and short those trending down, sizing each by 1/volatility, rebalanced monthly.
strategies.adapted_note: Single-stock futures proxied by spot stock returns.
